text: 🔥🇲🇽 The money García Luna stole is going to build schools in Mexico's poorest mountains. "Our goal is for this money to go to schools in La Montaña de Guerrero — for the areas of greatest need in the country." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 31 $5.8 million recovered from the Weinberg family — tied to jailed ex-security chief Genaro García Luna — reached Mexico's treasury Aug 25, from a forfeited bond and 12 liquidated Florida properties. It now funds high schools and universities in La Montaña de Guerrero.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>The World Cup left Mexico $2.5 billion</u>

The 2026 World Cup delivered Mexico a $2,543-million-dollar economic impact — 0.12% of GDP and 101,255 temporary jobs — with gastronomy alone adding $584M in sales and Mexico City leading at $548M, per Deloitte's study reported by El Economista. Tourism Secretary Josefina Rodríguez, to the doubters: "It did have an impact; our job now is to turn it into permanent benefits."

🇲🇽📚 <u>Mexico's first school year where every public-school kid has a scholarship</u>

The 2026-2027 school year is the first with universal scholarship coverage from primary through high school — 22.8 million students, up 217% from the 7.2 million supported in 2019, backed by 178.2 billion pesos. Sheinbaum, rejecting merit-only aid: "We don't want anyone to leave school for an economic reason. The classroom should not be a space for differentiation."

🇲🇽✊ <u>Sheinbaum takes teacher-evaluation reform straight to the teachers</u>

After failing to reach a deal with the CNTE, Sheinbaum will consult teachers directly, nationwide, on the future of USICAMM, the teacher-career system: "The consultation will be with them, directly, no intermediaries." She rejected the union's push to revive the pre-2013 mixed commissions — which, she said, "led to tremendous corruption" — favoring peer evaluation modeled on UNAM.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>'Alito' clings to the PRI — and its 800-million-peso purse</u>

PRI boss "Alito" Moreno is fighting to keep his party leadership — and the 800 million pesos a year in public financing the INE hands the PRI, which even PRI elder Francisco Labastida says drives his reelection "purely for personal interest." Prosecutors tie Moreno to 83.5 million pesos diverted while he was governor of Campeche, with two of his associates already jailed this August and properties surfacing in Texas.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Ebrard: Mexico came through the worst of US protectionism</u>

"Mexico has come through" the biggest foreign-trade challenge of the century, Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard says — after 20 direct Sheinbaum–Trump calls and weeks in Washington pressing to cut US tariffs on Mexican steel, aluminum and autos, he reports advances "close to very substantive agreements."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum sends Congress 11 priority reforms</u>

Sheinbaum's government just handed Morena's deputies 11 priority reforms for September: femicide homologated as a crime nationwide (she's proposed penalties of up to 70 years), an anti-corruption package rewriting 19 laws plus two new statutes, and an ISR reform to end the "aggressive tax planning" that let big companies pay just 2–3% of the tax they owe.

LATIN TIMES: "Sheinbaum Delivers Her Second Report Card — Here's the Fine Print Mexican Diaspora Families Need"
August 29, 2026 | 🟢

A rare US-outlet explainer that centers the diaspora, not the drug war. It relays Sheinbaum's numbers straight: irregular migration down ~97.5% from its peak, remittances near 3.5% of GDP. The squeeze it names is on the US side — Trump's 1% remittance excise tax, live since Jan. 1, hitting cash and money-order transfers home.

For 40 million people of Mexican descent in the US, it frames Washington's banking rules — not Mexico City's — as the thing to watch.

• migration "fallen roughly 97.5% from its peak"
• remittances "close to 3.5% of Mexico's entire economic output"

BORDERREPORT/CNN: "Key financial operator for Sinaloa cartel's Chapitos faction arrested, DEA says"
August 30, 2026 | 🟡

The capture happened in Mexicali, by Mexican forces — security chief Omar García Harfuch announced the arrest of Salvador "El Gusano" Díaz. The headline credits "DEA says." DEA administrator Terry Cole called it work "on both sides of the border"; the byline puts one side first.

Harfuch said the operation came from Mexican intelligence and investigative work — a line that lands below the DEA in the US retelling.

CBS/AFP: Tigers, jaguars, bison among 135 exotic animals "found in raid on fuel smugglers"
August 28, 2026 | 🟡

CBS leads with a cartel zoo — Bengal tigers, a camel, an American bison. The actual operation: Mexican marines dismantling a huachicol fuel-theft ring in Tamaulipas, seizing 18,000 gallons of stolen diesel, pumps and tanks. The exotic animals were incidental; the fuel bust — cartels' #2 revenue stream per the US Treasury — was the point.

The raid was Mexican forces' work, but no Mexican official is quoted; the spectacle gets the headline, the security win gets a clause.

• "rescued Bengal tigers, mandrills, hyenas and even a camel"
• victims "fed dead or alive to tigers"
